headline: Sony revives legendary WH-1000XM4 headphones with minor updates
summary: The acclaimed noise-canceling headphones return with a new 'C' designation, updated EQ, and Bluetooth 6 support, but with slightly reduced battery life.
details: Sony is bringing back its highly-regarded WH-1000XM4 noise-canceling headphones, six years after their initial release. The new model, dubbed the WH-1000XM4C, retains the original's iconic compact design and folding capabilities, which Sony had previously moved away from with the XM5.

While the exterior remains largely the same, with the addition of a lavender color option, the XM4C feature updated sound profiling to match current Sony models. They also gain a 10-band EQ in the Headphones app, up from the original's 5-band, and include a gaming preset. Bluetooth has been upgraded to version 6.

Interestingly, battery performance sees a slight decrease. The XM4C are rated for up to 27 hours of use with ANC on, compared to the original's 30 hours. Internally, they still utilize the QN1 processing chip and four microphones for ANC, a step down from the newer XM5 and XM6 models which feature more microphones and advanced processing chips.

The WH-1000XM4C are set to launch later this fall with a price tag of $300. This is $50 less than the original XM4's launch price and $100 cheaper than the current XM6 model, though more expensive than they could be found for before being discontinued.

Alongside the XM4C, Sony also refreshed its WH-CH730N and WH-CH530 headphone lines. Both receive the 10-band EQ upgrade, with the CH730N now featuring a more compact folding design. Battery life is significantly boosted on these models, with the CH730N offering up to 50 hours with ANC and the CH530 up to 55 hours without ANC.

New safety features include a volume limiting mode in the app, designed to protect younger users' hearing, though it lacks a lock function. The WH-CH530 will cost $70 and the WH-CH730N will be $180, with both available now in various color options. Sony is also releasing limited edition Hello Kitty bundles later this year.

headline_marked: Apple Wallet [[splits bills]] and adds passes using Visual Intelligence in iOS 27
headline: Apple Wallet splits bills and adds passes using Visual Intelligence in iOS 27
summary: The upcoming iOS 27 update introduces Visual Intelligence to Apple Wallet, allowing users to scan receipts for bill splitting and add physical passes directly.
details: Apple's iOS 27 update is bringing a new feature called Visual Intelligence to the Wallet app, designed to streamline group dining and pass management. This tool uses the iPhone's camera to recognize receipts, enabling users to split bills and send Apple Cash requests to friends.

To use the split bill feature, users must have Apple Cash set up and an itemized receipt that the camera can read. The Visual Intelligence feature aims to parse receipts for individual items, allowing for more accurate bill splitting than simply dividing the total cost.

Beyond bill splitting, Visual Intelligence will also assist in adding physical passes to Apple Wallet. By scanning compatible items like boarding passes, loyalty cards, or tickets, users can add them to their digital wallet, simplifying the process of managing various passes.

Visual Intelligence is accessible via the Control Center. Once added, users can tap the 'Split Bill with Apple Cash' button when it appears after scanning a receipt or scan physical passes for addition to Wallet. The feature is currently available in the iOS 27 Public or Developer Beta and will be officially released later this fall.

While Visual Intelligence offers a convenient fallback for adding passes, Apple notes that using the issuer's official 'Add to Apple Wallet' link or process may still yield more dependable results for certain passes.
